issues.legal_issue: A landlord's genuine intention to start or expand a business may establish bona fide need for eviction even when the landlord already conducts business elsewhere and some family members pursue other activities.
material_facts: The landlords established that a qualified son wanted to start a computer institute in the premises at Calicut and that other family members wanted to expand their business there.
The landlords already had business interests in Chennai and Hyderabad, and one son had settled in the United States.
The appellate authority, after considering the evidence, found the need genuine; the High Court affirmed that finding.
The Supreme Court found no basis to treat the concurrent findings as perverse or unsupported.
issues.conclusion: The bona fide need was established, and the eviction order on that ground was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11(3) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, the landlord's genuine need for own occupation may support eviction. The landlord may choose the nature and location of a business, and a tenant cannot dictate that choice. Existing business elsewhere does not by itself make a proposed expansion in another place sham or unreasonable. The Court relied on Ramkubai v. Hajarimal Dhokalchand Chandak, (1999) 6 SCC 540, in recognizing that a landlord need not remain idle pending litigation, and on the principles in Pratap Rai Tanwani v. Uttam Chand, (2004) 8 SCC 490, and Gaya Prasad v. Pradeep Srivastava, (2001) 2 SCC 604, concerning the date for assessing need and intervening events.

predicates.tenant_appeal_from_need_eviction: A tenant appealed an eviction order granted on the landlord's asserted need for own occupation.
predicates.genuine_business_plan_supported_by_evide: The landlord presented evidence of a genuine intention to start or expand a business in the premises.
predicates.supported_concurrent_findings: The lower courts' findings supporting the landlord's need were based on evidence and were not shown to be perverse.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals a need-based eviction order, evidence of a genuine business plan and supported concurrent findings result in the eviction order being upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord's bona fide need is ordinarily assessed as of the eviction petition, and events during prolonged litigation displace that assessment only when they completely eclipse the need.
material_facts: The landlords sought the premises to start or expand business, and the courts below found the need genuine when the eviction claim was brought.
The litigation continued for a prolonged period, during which the landlords and their sons could not be expected to remain idle.
One son had settled in the United States, but other sons still wanted to expand business at Calicut; the Court found that circumstance did not eclipse the need.
issues.conclusion: The need was properly assessed by reference to the date of the eviction petition; the later circumstances shown did not extinguish it.
issues.legal_principle: The normal rule is that parties' rights and obligations are determined as of the date of the eviction petition. Under the principles in Pratap Rai Tanwani v. Uttam Chand, (2004) 8 SCC 490, and Gaya Prasad v. Pradeep Srivastava, (2001) 2 SCC 604, later events may be considered when moulding relief, but only where their nature and dimension completely eclipse the landlord's need. A landlord should not be penalized for delays in the legal process.

rule.if: need_based_eviction_proceeding and need_existed_when_petition_filed and not later_event_completely_eclipsed_need

predicates.need_based_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns eviction sought on the landlord's asserted bona fide need.
predicates.need_existed_when_petition_filed: The landlord's asserted need existed when the eviction petition was filed.
predicates.later_event_completely_eclipsed_need: An event occurring during the litigation completely extinguished the landlord's asserted need.

issues.definition: If a need-based eviction proceeding began with an existing need and no later event completely extinguished it, the need is assessed as of the petition's filing.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant claiming protection based on occupation before the statutory cutoff cannot rely on a predecessor partnership's occupation after a voluntary incorporation unless the tenant proves that the old and new entities were essentially the same.
material_facts: The premises had been occupied by a partnership firm before the tenant company was incorporated in 1948.

The tenant company claimed protection based on occupation predating the statutory cutoff, but did not produce specific evidence that the old firm's partners continued as the company's directors or members.
The lower courts found that the company was a separate legal entity and that its tenancy began in 1948; the Supreme Court found no evidentiary basis to disturb those concurrent findings.
The tenant relied on facts from another case, but the Court held that it had to plead and prove the relevant facts in this proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The tenant company did not qualify for the statutory protection and could be evicted on the landlord's bona fide need.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11(17) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965 protects a tenant in continuous occupation from 1 April 1940 against eviction for the landlord's bona fide occupation, subject to the section's stated exception. Where a business is voluntarily transferred to a newly incorporated entity, the tenant must plead and prove that the members of the old firm continued in the new entity and that it is essentially the same; a statutory transfer is an exception. The Court considered Madras Bangalore Transport Co. (West) v. Inder Singh, (1986) 3 SCC 62; Singer India Ltd. v. Chander Mohan Chadha, (2004) 7 SCC 1; Electrical Cable Development Association v. Arun Commercial Premises Cooperative Housing Society Ltd., (1998) 5 SCC 396; G. Sridharamurti v. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd., (1995) 6 SCC 605; and the other cited authorities on identity between predecessor and successor entities and the need to prove the relevant facts.

rule.if: tenant_appeal_from_need_eviction and predecessor_occupied_before_cutoff and voluntary_entity_conversion and not continuity_of_members_proven and not conversion_imposed_by_law

predicates.tenant_appeal_from_need_eviction: A tenant appealed an eviction order granted on the landlord's asserted bona fide need.
predicates.predecessor_occupied_before_cutoff: A predecessor business entity occupied the premises as tenant before the statutory cutoff.
predicates.voluntary_entity_conversion: The tenant's business was transferred to or continued through a voluntarily formed new entity.
predicates.continuity_of_members_proven: The tenant proved that the members of the predecessor continued in the new entity so that the entities were essentially the same.
predicates.conversion_imposed_by_law: A statute or other law imposed the transfer or conversion to the new entity.

issues.definition: When a predecessor occupied the premises before the cutoff but a voluntary new entity cannot prove continuity of membership, and the change was not imposed by law, the claimed occupation-based protection is unavailable in the need-based eviction appeal.
